sources.quote: 'Tone interacts with stress placement in Uspanteko. In toneless words, stress falls on the final syllable, as in 1. There is no secondary stress.' ex.(1a) tinach'ab'eej [ti.na.tʃˀa.ˈɓeːχ]; 'Stress and tone are phonetically separable in Uspanteko: stress is primarily cued by duration'; 'stress retracts to the penult to coincide' with H on a short-vowel-final tonal word; adopts B&H 2013 iambic-by-default foot analysis.

sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan, Robert Henderson & Meg Harvey. 2022. Tonal variability and marginal contrast: Lexical pitch accent in Uspanteko. In H. Kubozono, J. Ito & A. Mester (eds.), Prosody and prosodic interfaces, 187-226. Oxford: OUP. (author preprint from people.ucsc.edu/~rbennett)
sources.quote: 'The basic stress system of Uspanteko is straightforward. In toneless words, stress falls on the word-final syllable, essentially without exception. There are no secondary stresses. ... the same pattern of stress assignment found in other K'ichean-branch Mayan languages' ; 'long vowels are restricted to stressed, word-final syllables'; in tonal words with a final short vowel 'tone is realized on the penultimate syllable, and stress retracts to the position of' tone; 'stress retraction is specifically driven by H tone because this is the only context in which penultimate stress is ever observed

sources.quote: 'El acento tónico normalmente ocurre al final de palabra, aunque el acento se retrae a la penúltima sílaba en palabras con vocales tonales cortas'; p.133: 'En todas las otras lenguas k'icheanas, el acento recae casi siempre en la sílaba final, sin condicionamiento por longitud vocálica o peso de la sílaba'.

sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan, Robert Henderson & Meg Harvey. 2019. The interaction of tone and intonation in Uspanteko. Proceedings of ICPhS 2019, 452-456. Canberra: ASSTA.
sources.quote: 'Lexical tone in Uspanteko is overlaid on a system of stress and vowel length familiar from related languages. Stress in non-tonal words is final (e.g. kaminaq [ka.mi.ˈnaqh] 'dead'). Contrastive long vowels only occur in word-final stressed syllables ... In a word with a final short vowel, like wíxk'eq, lexical tone appears on the penult, and stress retracts to the same position. ... stress is associated with increased duration, while tone is associated with pitch raising'.
